find: const mines: Mine[] = world.mines.filter((m) => MINE_TIMER - m.timer >= lag);
replace: const mines: Mine[] = world.mines.filter((m) => MINE_TIMER - m.timer >= 0);
why: The FUSE-STATE half of the perceived picture goes, leaving the shell back-dating behind: every mine is noticed the instant it is dropped, however stale the tank's picture of everything else is. That is the one-dimensional error issue #223 names as the defect ("not only a fresh radius offset") reintroduced on the mine side alone, and it survives every shell-based fixture in the file by construction. The replacement keeps the same filter shape with a zero threshold rather than deleting the predicate, so it is a threshold regression rather than an obviously-dead line. Killed by the single test that owns the claim, which asserts both directions -- a mine younger than the delay is absent, one older is present -- plus the inclusive boundary at exactly the delay.
killedBy: backdateHazards: the stale picture itself hides a mine younger than the delay and keeps an older one -- perceived FUSE STATE
